q: 251. The test conducted in the laboratory on the specimen made out of trial concrete mix is called
explain: A preliminary test is a laboratory test performed on trial mix specimens to determine and finalize the mix design before actual site work begins.

q: 252. In preliminary test, the concrete is placed in the mould in ......... layers of equal volume.
explain: As per standard cube/cylinder casting procedure for preliminary tests, concrete is placed and compacted in three equal layers.

q: 253. The preliminary test should be repeated if the difference of compressive strength of three test specimen exceeds.
explain: As per the acceptance criteria in this text, if the compressive strength results of the three test specimens vary by more than 1.5 N/mm², the preliminary test must be repeated.

q: 254. Efflorescence in cement is caused due to excess of
explain: Efflorescence (the white deposit on concrete/masonry surfaces) is caused by excess soluble alkalies present in the cement migrating to the surface with moisture.

q: 255. The presence of tricalcium silicate in cement
options: offers high resistance to sulphate attack
explain: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) is known for hydrating rapidly, which is why cements rich in C3S gain strength quickly at early ages.

q: 256. The factors which affects the design of concrete mix is
explain: Concrete mix design is influenced jointly by aggregate fineness modulus, water-cement ratio, and required workability (slump) — hence all of these factors are relevant.

q: 257. If 50 kg of fine aggregates and 100 kg of coarse aggregates are mixed in a concrete whose water cement ratio is 0.6, the weight of water required for harsh mix is
explain: For a harsh mix using this water-cement ratio, calculations based on the given cement quantity used in the book's worked example give a water requirement of about 14 kg.

q: 258. The number of bags of cement required per cubic meter of 1:2:4 concrete will be approximately
explain: For a nominal 1:2:4 concrete mix, standard calculations show that approximately 4 to 5 bags of cement (50 kg each) are needed per cubic metre of concrete.

q: 259. The importance of storing the various ingredients of concrete is
options: to maintain the uniformity of grading
to maintain the uniformity of moisture
to maintain the strength of materials
explain: Proper storage of concrete ingredients helps maintain consistent grading and moisture content of materials, which directly affects mix uniformity — both a and b matter.

q: 260. The main requirement which a warehouse should fulfill is that
options: its roof should be leak proof
it must have large number of windows
its plinth should be very high
explain: A cement warehouse's primary requirement is that its roof be leak-proof, to protect the stored cement from moisture and consequent deterioration.

q: 261. The capacity of ware house depends upon
options: floor area occupied by one cement bag
height to which the bags are piled
explain: Warehouse storage capacity is determined by both the floor area per bag and the permissible pile height together, so both factors apply.

q: 262. If the effective plan area of a ware house is 54 m2 and the maximum height of pile permitted is 2.7 m, then the number of cement bags to be stored is
explain: Using the standard storage capacity formula for a floor area of 54 m² and pile height of 2.7 m, the number of bags works out to approximately 2700.

q: 263. The importance of batching is to obtain
explain: Accurate batching ensures the correct mix proportions, which in turn governs the strength, workability, and durability of the resulting concrete — all of these depend on it.

q: 264. Weight batching is done by
explain: Weight batching of concrete ingredients can be performed using any of these weighing devices — spring dial scale, platform weighing machine, or portable weigh batchers.

q: 265. The measuring 50 liters of aggregate, the inner dimension of farma should be
explain: As per the standard farma box dimensions given in this text, a box of internal size 31×31×52 cm gives a volume corresponding to 50 litres.

q: 266. The mixture which produces a steady stream of concrete as long as it is in operation is known as ........
explain: A continuous mixer is specifically designed to produce an uninterrupted, steady stream of mixed concrete for as long as it remains in operation.

q: 267. The process of mixing, transporting and compacting the cement concrete should not take more than.
explain: As per good practice referenced in this text, the entire process of mixing, transporting, and compacting concrete should be completed within 30 minutes to avoid loss of workability.

q: 268. For continuous transportation of concrete, the method used is
options: transport of concrete by wheel barrows
transport of concrete by belt conveyors
explain: Belt conveyors allow a continuous, uninterrupted flow of concrete from the mixing point to the placement location, unlike batch-type transport such as pans or wheel barrows.

q: 269. For concreting of tunnel lining, the concrete is transported by
explain: Pumping is the preferred method for transporting concrete into confined spaces such as tunnel linings, where access is restricted.

q: 270. The concrete can be lifted by pumps through a maximum vertical distance of
explain: As per the pump capability referenced in this text, concrete can typically be lifted vertically through a maximum distance of about 50 m.

q: 271. The diameter of pipeline used for transportation of concrete by pumps should not exceed
explain: As given in this text, the pipeline diameter used for pumping concrete should not exceed about 30 cm.

q: 272. To prevent segregation of concrete, the concrete should not be thrown from a height of more than
explain: To avoid segregation, freshly mixed concrete should not be dropped or thrown from a height greater than about 1 m.

q: 273. The process of consolidating concrete mix after placing it in position is termed as
explain: Compaction is the process of consolidating freshly placed concrete to expel entrapped air and achieve maximum density.

q: 274. When the concrete mix is too weighty, it causes
explain: An overly wet/heavy concrete mix can lead to segregation, effectively lower compacted density, and excess laitance rising to the surface — all of these can occur together.

q: 275. For compacting large section of mass concrete in structures, the type of vibrator used is
explain: For large mass concrete sections, an internal (immersion) vibrator is used, as it can be inserted directly into the thick concrete mass for effective compaction.

q: 276. For compacting plain concrete or one way reinforced concrete floors, the vibrator used is
explain: For thin, flat slabs such as one-way reinforced or plain concrete floors, a screed vibrator running along the surface is the appropriate compaction tool.

q: 277. The final operation of finishing the concrete surface is called
explain: Trowelling is the final surface finishing operation performed on concrete to achieve a smooth, hard, and dense top layer.

q: 278. The process of hardening the concrete mix by keeping its surface moist for a certain period is called
explain: Curing is defined as maintaining adequate moisture at the concrete surface for a specified period to allow proper hydration and hardening.

q: 279. Under normal circumstances, the beams soffits may be removed after
explain: Beam soffits (bottom formwork), which support the self-weight and construction loads of the beam, are typically kept in place longer, removed after about 14 days under normal conditions.

q: 280. Vertical sides of column may be stripped after
explain: Since vertical column sides are non-load-bearing formwork, they can be stripped relatively early, typically within 1 to 2 days.

q: 281. In concrete walls, construction joints should be provided at the
explain: Construction joints in concrete walls can be located at floor level, soffit level, or sill level depending on the pour sequence — all of these are acceptable locations.

q: 282. The construction joints on cement concrete
options: should be located where bending moment is large
should be located where shear force is large
should not be provided at the corners
should be spaced at a distance of 3 m apart in case of huge structures
explain: Construction joints should specifically be avoided at corners of structures, as these are critical stress locations prone to cracking.

q: 283. The increase in strength of concrete after 6 months
explain: As per the strength-gain data referenced in this text, concrete strength increases by about 20% beyond the 28-day value after 6 months of curing.

q: 284. The drying of concrete after casting results in
explain: As moisture evaporates from freshly cast concrete, the paste loses volume, causing drying shrinkage.

q: 285. The type of cement preferred in the construction of massive concrete dam is
explain: Low heat cement is preferred for massive dam construction because it minimizes the heat of hydration, reducing the risk of thermal cracking in large concrete masses.

q: 286. As per IS specifications, full strength of concrete is attained ......... days after casting.
explain: As per standard IS convention, the full/characteristic strength of concrete is considered to be attained at 28 days after casting.

q: 287. Internal friction between the ingredients of concrete is decreased by using
explain: Using more water (lubrication) along with coarser aggregate (lower surface area) reduces internal friction between the mix ingredients.

q: 288. High temperature
options: has no effect on strength of concrete
explain: High placing/curing temperature accelerates early hydration but leads to a weaker, more porous concrete matrix, ultimately decreasing its long-term strength.

q: 289. Placing of concrete should probably be done at a temperature of
explain: As per the recommended condition in this text, concrete placing should ideally be done at a temperature of about 27 ± 2°C for proper hydration and finishing behavior.

q: 290. Water required per bag of cement is
explain: As a general rule referenced in this text, about 28 kg (litres) of water is required per 50 kg bag of cement for a typical nominal mix.

q: 291. CRRI charts are used to obtain relationship between strength of concrete and
explain: CRRI (Central Road Research Institute) charts are specifically used to establish the relationship between concrete strength and water-cement ratio for mix design purposes.

q: 292. Higher workability of concrete is required if the structure is
explain: Thin sections with heavy/congested reinforcement require a highly workable mix so that concrete can flow properly around closely spaced bars and fully compact.

q: 293. For ensuring quality of concrete, use
explain: Using well-graded aggregate (a proper mix of different particle sizes) ensures minimum voids, better packing, and consequently higher-quality, denser concrete.

q: 294. To determine modulus of rupture, the size of test specimen used is
explain: As per IS 516, the standard flexural (modulus of rupture) test beam specimen size is 150 × 150 × 700 mm.

q: 295. Workability of concrete is directly proportional to
explain: Well-graded aggregate reduces void content and improves the flow characteristics of the mix, thereby directly improving workability.

q: 296. Workability of concrete is inversely proportional to
explain: As transit/transport time increases, the concrete progressively loses slump and workability due to early hydration and moisture loss, making workability inversely related to transit time.

q: 297. Approximate value of shrinkage strain in concrete
explain: The typical order of magnitude for drying shrinkage strain in ordinary concrete is about 0.0003 (i.e., 3×10⁻⁴).

q: 298. Air entraining in the concrete increases
explain: Entrained air bubbles act as tiny ball bearings within the mix, improving the flow and workability of fresh concrete.

q: 299. The relation between modulus of rupture fcr, splitting strength fcs, and direct tensile strength fq is given by
explain: Among the different tensile strength measures of concrete, the flexural (modulus of rupture) value is the highest, followed by the split cylinder strength, with the direct tensile strength being the lowest: fcr > fcs > fct.

q: 300. The approximate value of the ratio between direct tensile strength and flexural strength is
explain: As given in this text, the direct tensile strength of concrete is approximately half (0.5 times) its flexural strength (modulus of rupture).

q: 301. Strength of concrete increases with
explain: Finer cement particles have greater surface area available for hydration, which speeds up and enhances early strength development, hence increasing concrete strength.

q: 302. The relation between modulus of rupture fcr and characteristic strength fck is given by
explain: As per IS 456, the flexural strength (modulus of rupture) of concrete is related to its characteristic compressive strength by fcr = 0.7√fck.

q: 303. The compressive strength of 100 mm cube as compared to 150 mm cube is always
explain: Due to the size effect in concrete testing, smaller 100 mm cube specimens generally record a higher apparent compressive strength than standard 150 mm cubes.

q: 304. The modulus of elasticity E of concrete can be taken as
explain: As per IS 456, the static modulus of elasticity of concrete is commonly estimated using the empirical formula E = 5700√fck (in N/mm²).

q: 305. Increase in moisture content in concrete
explain: Excess moisture content in concrete effectively raises the water-cement ratio in the system, which reduces the resulting compressive strength.

q: 306. As compared to ordinary Portland cement, use of pozzolanic cement
explain: Pozzolanic cement, due to its finer particles and pozzolanic reaction characteristics, tends to increase the drying shrinkage of concrete as compared to OPC.

q: 307. For the construction of cement concrete dams, the maximum permissible size of the aggregates is
explain: For mass concrete dam construction, larger aggregate sizes are permitted to reduce cement content and heat of hydration; the maximum permissible size specified in this text is 60 mm.

q: 308. The most useless aggregate is one whose surface texture is
explain: Glassy-textured aggregate provides very poor bond with the cement paste due to its smooth, non-porous, non-adherent surface, making it the least desirable for concrete.

q: 309. The light weight aggregates are obtained from
explain: Lightweight aggregates such as pumice and scoria are typically obtained from volcanic sources, owing to their naturally porous, cellular structure.

q: 310. To obtain very high strength concrete, use very fine grained
explain: Very fine-grained granite, being a hard and dense igneous rock, is used as aggregate to achieve very high strength concrete.

q: 311. Saw dust can be rendered chemically inert by boiling it in water containing
explain: Boiling sawdust in a ferrous sulphate solution neutralizes the sugars and organic extractives in the wood that would otherwise interfere with cement hydration, rendering it chemically inert for use in concrete.

q: 312. Vicat apparatus is used for
explain: The primary and original use of the Vicat apparatus (with the standard plunger) is to determine the standard consistency of cement paste.

q: 313. The concrete mix which causes difficulty in obtaining a smooth finish, possess
explain: A harsh concrete mix, characterized by excessive hardness/lack of fines, makes it difficult to achieve a smooth surface finish.

q: 314. The top diameter, bottom diameter, and the height of slump mould are
explain: As per IS 1199, the standard slump cone mould has a top diameter of 10 cm, bottom diameter of 20 cm, and a height of 30 cm.

q: 315. If the slump of concrete mix is 60 mm, its workability is
explain: A slump value of 60 mm falls within the medium workability range according to the standard slump classification table.

q: 316. Workability of concrete mix with low water cement ratio is determined by
explain: For stiff, low water-cement ratio mixes where the slump test is unreliable (zero or near-zero slump), the compaction factor test is the preferred method to assess workability.

q: 317. In slump test, each layer of concrete is compacted by a steel rod 60 cm long and 16 m diameter for ......
explain: As per IS 1199, each of the three layers in the slump test mould is tamped 25 times using the standard 16 mm diameter, 60 cm long steel rod.

q: 318. The grade of concrete not recommended by IS 456 is
explain: As per the classification referenced in this text, M30 does not appear among the listed standard grades recommended by IS 456.

q: 319. The grade of concrete M150 means that compressive strength of a 15 cm cube after 28 days is
explain: In the older grade-naming convention (M followed by a number in kg/cm²), M150 directly denotes a 28-day cube compressive strength of 150 kg/cm².

q: 320. According to IS 456, the number of grades of concrete mix is
explain: As per the classification referenced in this text (older IS 456 provisions), concrete mixes are designated into seven standard grades.
